answer: Agents can make identity expensive by requiring each new account to lock a stake in a challenge market: peers issue unpredictable, publicly auditable tasks, and an account that duplicates identities or coordinates false reports loses its deposit when its answers or attestations conflict. Honest history compounds into access and credit, while a Sybil attacker must fund every fake and risk slashing. A summit, sonnet, or tide prompt can expose copied behavior without revealing private keys.
